tldr: Headlines across the six-country corpus frame this as a health emergency anchored by body counts and unprecedented official warnings: international outlets (Turkey, Germany, Pakistan, Malaysia) lead with South Korea's 16 heat deaths and a 122-year temperature record, while South Korean domestic outlets foreground the escalating warning system — Seoul's first-ever citywide highest-level heat alert — and President Lee's declaration of a national disaster. Italy's concurrent heatwave (23 of 27 major cities on red alert) appears only via ANSA, unconnected to the South Korea coverage.

single_outlet_findings.finding: The only outlet covering Italy's fourth heatwave of 2026 rather than South Korea's — 23 of 27 major cities on red alert — making the Italy bucket an entirely self-contained national emergency rather than a lens on the South Korea story; no outlet in the corpus synthesizes the two concurrent crises at the headline layer.

Only headline in the corpus to frame the heatwave through an economic-regulatory lens — industrial electricity bill revision — absent from all international outlets and all other domestic Korean headlines, which focus exclusively on alerts and fatalities.

Only headline to introduce a compound weather risk — an approaching typhoon — as a source of uncertainty about the prolonged heat wave, adding a forecasting dimension absent from all other domestic and international headlines in the corpus.

bottom_line: At the headline layer, international outlets uniformly lead with South Korea's 16 heat deaths and a 122-year temperature record while domestic outlets foreground the first-ever citywide Seoul warning and a presidential disaster declaration — a clean inside-out split with no outlet crossing both registers.
